Subject: Renewal: Priority Retainer & Premium SLA — initial proposal

Hi Alex and Maya,

Hope you’re both well. Your annual subscription is coming up on 2026-11-15; thanks again for the productive year and the usage growth we’ve seen. Based on the volume and the regional failover needs you described in Q2, we put together two renewal paths that we think cover the priorities you flagged in the QBR: predictable latency tail protection and a named on-call path for incidents.

Attached is a term sheet with the items we recommend:
- Premium SLA (99.95% uptime, 95th/99th token latency SLOs by route)
- Priority retainer (24/7 on-call with 2-hour response for Sev 1)
- Optional seat swap: convert some of your unused developer seats into extended retainer hours at a discounted uplift

High-level commercial: ~18% uplift vs current list for the premium SLA + retainer (we factored committed monthly tokens). I included an ops handoff template (spreadsheet) so we can capture the on-call ROIs and escalation contacts.

Can you confirm interest in the premium SLA + retainer path? If so, we’ll send a redlineable term sheet and a DocuSign for signatures. If procurement wants a lower-cost option, we can also bake in a staged latency ladder (tiered SLOs during spikes).

Suggested next steps:
1) Customer confirmation of preferred path (premium vs staged) — by 2026-10-06
2) Internal pricing approval + redline (we can loop finance) — by 2026-10-09
3) Execute term sheet and schedule ops onboarding call (2 weeks pre-renewal)

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync if helpful.

Best,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear options and the template. Quick notes from our side after a brief sync with Maya and procurement:

- We want the Premium SLA (latency guarantees are important for our customer-facing search flows), but procurement will push back on a straight 18% uplift.
- The seat-swap idea is interesting: we have ~12 dev seats not being used consistently; converting 6 of those to extended retainer hours sounds viable.
- Two asks before we can push to legal: 1) a short clause that allows a one-time trial of the premium SLOs for 30 days post-signing with an opt-out if SLOs materially miss targets; 2) clarity on regional failover (what happens to latency SLOs during a cross-region failover).

Can you have Ben or Marissa outline the trial wording and the failover behavior? Procurement wants clear, short bullets they can send to legal.

- Alex

Subject: Re: Renewal: Priority Retainer & Premium SLA — trial & failover wording

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Quick internal summary / proposal below for procurement/legal-friendly bullets. Hannah, please adjust pricing if we accept the seat-swap.

Trial clause (30-day verification):
- Upon execution, Redwood will operate the account under Premium SLA settings for 30 days (trial period). During trial, Redwood will monitor baseline SLOs and provide a verification report at day 30.
- If the account experiences a material SLO miss (>10% of measured requests exceeding 99th latency threshold) attributable to Redwood runtime (not customer prompt patterns or changed traffic model), customer may elect to: (a) continue with a negotiated credit equal to one-third of one month’s retainer; or (b) revert to the prior SLA and receive a prorated refund of retainer fees for the trial month.

Regional failover behavior (short bullets):
- Latency SLOs are defined per-active-region. During automatic cross-region failover, Redwood provides a 72-hour mitigation window where token-based penalties are held in abeyance while the system rebalances caches.
- If failover persists beyond 72 hours and measurable SLOs are missed attributable to Redwood capacity routing, customer is eligible for credit per the SLA credit matrix (see term sheet).

Seat-swap pricing note:
- If customer converts N unused developer seats into retainer hours at renewal, we’ll apply a 30% discount on the hourly rate for those hours for the first 6 months. Hannah — if you confirm N=6 we’ll update the sheet and recalc ARR uplift.

Next steps: I’ll put a redline-friendly snippet into the term sheet and attach for legal to review. Hannah — can you confirm whether procurement prefers credits or a contract-level cap on remediation?

—Ben

Thanks Ben — that language looks much better and addresses the procurement concerns. A few quick confirmations from our side:

1) We will convert 6 developer seats into retainer hours (please update the pricing).
2) We accept the 30-day verification trial with the remedial options outlined (procurement prefers the prorated refund option if we exercise the opt-out).
3) The 72-hour mitigation window for cross-region failover is acceptable; please ensure the term sheet calls out the mechanism for initiating the mitigation window.

Procurement asks for a single redlineable PDF and DocuSign envelope we can circulate internally. Can you send that and flag the contract as: ClearNorth — Priority Retainer (Renewal) — Execution needed by 2026-10-20?

Once we have the DocuSign the CFO can route it. We’ll schedule the ops onboarding call after signatures.

Best,
